source.title: On Memorization in Probabilistic Deep Generative Models
source.citation: Gerrit J. J. van den Burg et al., 2021
source.authors: Gerrit J. J. van den Burg; C. Williams

page_placements.theme: Retained training information can escape aggregate performance diagnostics

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies memorization in probabilistic generative models, but does not test the claim’s random-label, unstructured-input, label-noise, regularization, or learning-order versions. Its references to those topics describe prior work.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own experiments measure memorization of real training observations in VAEs. Those results do not measure any listed claim version. The discussion of random-data learning and noisy-label memorization cites prior work and is not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures instance-level memorization in unsupervised VAEs through changes in observation likelihood when training observations are excluded. It does not test random-label fitting, fitting unstructured inputs, label-corruption effects, or learning order for real versus noisy labels. Its discussion of those findings cites prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: instance-level memorization in probabilistic generative models can coexist with generalization, arise before a generalization gap, and escape nearest-neighbor assessments. The authors also find that highly memorized observations need not be unlikely under the model.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures leave-one-out or cross-validated changes in probabilistic density for real observations in VAEs; it does not reproduce random-label fitting experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes the memorization-score distribution and maximum score; memorization quantiles also change over training.

fits_no_version.finding: MNIST VAE memorization quantiles increase during training and can become large before a generalization gap appears. Lowering the learning rate reduces the maximum score from about 210 to about 80.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instance-level memorization in probabilistic generative models can arise before a generalization gap and persist with a lower learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: The CelebA nearest-neighbor distance ratio has no strong correlation with the proposed memorization score.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nearest-neighbor distance ratios need not reliably track instance-level likelihood-based memorization in VAEs.

fits_no_version.finding: More than half of highly memorized CelebA observations fall within the central 90% of model log probabilities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Highly memorized observations in a VAE need not have low likelihood when included in training.

record.problems: The authors state that memorization scores are not necessarily comparable between data sets and that what constitutes a high score requires further study. Experimental settings were chosen partly for available computational resources and were not extensively optimized. Nearest-neighbor comparisons depend on a distance metric and sampling variability.
record.rows_left_out: No results were left out. The text also reports dataset-specific memorization-score ranges and medians in Figure 2 and Supplementary Figures 7–9; these are descriptive examples of score distributions and were not separately rowed because the table includes the study’s central results relevant to its own memorization findings.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting to zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true and random labels and convergence across label-corruption fractions.
Zero-error fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test performance across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: The cannot_determine states concern the listed claim versions, not the validity of the study's reported findings. No own result or specific argument tests V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Random labels, training and test error, architecture and hyperparameter changes.
Training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test performance across levels of label corruption.
Effects of regularization and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: VAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured memorization scores for observations across training epochs.
rows.value: Both quantiles increase during training; large values occur before the generalization gap appears, and the peak-quantile rate of increase slows with more training.
rows.note: Reports the quantile trend in the text; no exact quantile values are stated there.
rows.check: The reported trend is accurate, but likelihood-based memorization during unsupervised training cannot establish V6's ordering of real-label learning and noisy-label memorization.

rows.subject: VAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured memorization scores under a lower learning rate.
rows.value: Memorization scores are reduced; maximum about 80, with relatively high values still occurring.
rows.note: The text says the largest score represents a shift from a far outlier when absent to a central inlier when present.
rows.check: The maxima of about 210 and 80 are correctly reported. Reduced memorization scores under a lower learning rate do not measure any listed version; 'partial' is therefore inapplicable.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, lines 374–379 and 465–470; Figure 4 caption, lines 590–593.

rows.subject: VAE
rows.operation_detail: Compared memorization scores with a nearest-neighbor distance ratio.

conditions.value: Euclidean distance in pixel space after downsampling by a factor of 2

rows.measure: Relationship between memorization score and distance ratio ρi
rows.value: In general there is no strong correlation between the two score functions.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 5a error bars represent confidence intervals of the standard error of the mean for distance-ratio measurements in each bin.
rows.note: The authors explain that the scores measure different quantities.
rows.check: The lack of strong correlation is accurately reported, but comparison of two generative-model memorization measures cannot establish any listed version.

rows.subject: VAE
rows.operation_detail: Counted highly memorized observations across bins of log probability under the model.
rows.measure: Proportion of highly memorized observations within the central 90% of log probability values
rows.value: More than half the highly memorized observations fall within the central 90% of log probability values (i.e., with log PA (x | D) ∈ [−14500, −12000]).
rows.note: The paper reports that highly memorized observations are not necessarily unlikely under the model.
rows.check: The proportion and likelihood interval are accurately reported, but memorization of real observations in an unsupervised VAE does not measure any listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Section 4.2, lines 374–379 and 465–470; Figure 4 caption, lines 590–593.

relation.reason: Section 2 discusses learning random data and label-noise-induced memorization; the study neither tests nor uses random-label fitting.

tranche.reason: The study measures observation-level likelihood changes in unsupervised VAEs, a different construct from all six random-label claim versions.

source_check.notes: The authors’ conclusion paraphrase is accurate. Early likelihood-based memorization does not establish the ordering of real-label learning and noisy-label memorization in V6.
